vetting.label: ngc1333-a
vetting.note: Deep structure near 4.27 microns explains why different local wavelengths can mimic variability. Temporal interpretation rejected; no new molecular claim.

vetting.label: ngc1333-b
vetting.note: Source is blended with nearby ASR 42, which is the VSX-listed Gaia variable; that VSX match must not be assigned to this target. Continuum fading is also possible, but low-precision EPSF fits and blending prevent a clean attribution.

vetting.label: l1688-a
vetting.note: Two independent Aug16 exposures are fainter in nearby bands; earlier and March measurements agree. Survives multiple aperture radii and reference-star calibration. Known source; event novelty and cause unproven.

vetting.label: serpens-a
vetting.note: About 29.5% brightening at closely matched 4.255-micron wavelengths survives neighbour fitting and field calibration. Original WFCAM catalogue establishes prior variability despite absent VSX/Gaia matches.

vetting.label: serpens-b
vetting.note: Known YSO variable in Gaia and VSX. Infrared brightening is interesting, but not a new variable. Nearby source complicates precise deblending.

vetting.label: serpens-c
vetting.note: Fading near 1.571 microns. Gaia and VSX already identify variability. Not a new object or variable.

vetting.label: serpens-d
vetting.note: Known variable recovered; native apertures and EPSF fits show fading. Not a discovery.

vetting.label: serpens-e
vetting.note: Many infrared counterparts inside the aperture and strong wavelength dependence near 4.27 microns. Matched Mar-May EPSF flux is nearly unchanged. No isolated temporal discovery claim.

vetting.label: serpens-f
vetting.note: Known variable. The initial D5 wavelengths differ by nearly half a channel near 4.27 microns; the blind-screen amplitude is not a verified temporal amplitude.

vetting.label: ngc2264-a
vetting.note: Unresolved known young variable: native differential ratios 2.299 +/- 0.161 at 1.193 microns and 1.111 +/- 0.069 at 3.936 microns over the same two dates.

vetting.label: ngc2264-b
vetting.note: Known variable; native fits reproduce approximately 50% short-wavelength brightening. No novelty claim.

vetting.label: ngc2264-c
vetting.note: Known variable counterpart; nearby V820 Mon is a different star. Modest near-1.58-micron fading is not a new variable discovery.

vetting.label: orion-a
vetting.note: Park2021 classifies this counterpart as irregular. EPSF errors are about 13% with reduced chi-square >100; the stricter photometry gate rejects the nominal initial significance.

conclusion: Interesting variability and a promising candidate event in known sources; no established new object or proven novelty.
